subject: Career
title: The Double Opt-In Introduction
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Double Opt-In Introduction.

hook.text: She wanted to connect two people. Instead of cc-ing both, she asked each first. Consent before connection.

buildup.text: The double opt-in: ask both parties if they want to be introduced before making the introduction.

discovery.text: This protects both people's time and ensures the connection is welcomed, not imposed.

twist.text: Skipping the opt-in signals you value your generosity more than their time. It burns goodwill.

climax.text: Message each person separately: explain why you think they should connect and ask permission.

punchline.text: Great connectors ask permission first. Not overhead — respect.

quiz.question: What is a double opt-in introduction?
options: Asking both parties for consent before connecting them

details.summary: A double opt-in introduction checks with both parties privately before making the connection, ensuring mutual interest and consent. This approach respects everyone's time and preserves the introducer's credibility.
details.whyItMatters: Unsolicited introductions can annoy the recipient and damage the introducer's reputation. Double opt-in is the gold standard because it protects all three relationships in the chain.
takeaways: Ask each party separately before connecting them together
Share enough context for both sides to make an informed decision
Respect a no from either side without pressure

faq.question: When is it acceptable to skip the double opt-in and make a direct introduction?
faq.answer: Only when you are highly confident both parties would welcome the connection and the context is obviously beneficial. Even then, err toward double opt-in. The small extra effort protects relationships and demonstrates social sophistication.

faq.question: How do you handle it when one party declines a double opt-in introduction?
faq.answer: Thank them for their honesty and do not press further. Inform the requesting party that the timing was not right without sharing the specific reason for the decline. Gracious handling of a no preserves all relationships.
